GW-Trust-in-Scientists-Statements.pdf.notes: Examines public trust in environmental scientists, climate beliefs, and responses to mainstream and skeptical scientific messages.

alvarez_2023_trust_university_researcher.notes: Nationally representative survey (n=2,096) finds low trust in university research on climate is linked to denialism and calls for research on framing/messaging to build trust -- correlational, not a message-effect test.

bernauer_2016_reframing_climate_policy.p.notes: Tests economic, community, health, and climate-risk frames and finds limited gains from simple reframing.

besley_2017_conflict_interest.pdf.notes: Shows that industry involvement can reduce perceived legitimacy of scientific research partnerships.

brulle_2021_foundation_funding_countermo.notes: Institutional funding-flow analysis (2003-2018) of climate-countermovement organizations -- background context for the Funding/Oil industry misinformation stimuli, but tests no survey outcome itself.

cologna_2024_trust_review.pdf.notes: Narrative review of trust, reasons for distrust, political engagement, and trustworthy climate communication.

cologna_2025_trust_scientists_68.pdf.notes: Measures competence, benevolence, integrity, and openness across 68 countries and finds generally high trust.

cook_2017_inoculation.pdf.notes: Tests pre-emptive messages that explain misleading techniques or emphasize scientific consensus.

dasandi_2022_framing_public_support.pdf.notes: Finds positive, health, environmental, global, and immediate frames can increase climate-policy support.

fairbrother_2016_geoengineering_moral_ha.notes: Tests whether information about solar geoengineering changes trust or support for emissions-reduction policies.

fujimi_2021_trust_projection_formats.pdf.journal: Mitigation and Adaptation Strategies for Global Change
fujimi_2021_trust_projection_formats.pdf.notes: Compares average, range, and multi-value climate-projection formats and their effects on trust and concern.

galdikiene_2026_pluralistic_ignorance.pd.notes: Corrects perceived public support for carbon taxation and finds mixed effects, including possible donation backfire.

goerg_2024_social_norm_nudges.pdf.notes: Shows that national norm information can increase policy support while regional norms may be ineffective or backfire.

goldberg_2021_republican_advertising.pdf.notes: Tests targeted climate advertising and finds increased Republican understanding of climate existence, causes, and harms.

goldfarb_kriner_2017_public_support_scie.notes: Randomized correction telling respondents the true (low, ~1%) share of the federal budget spent on science shifts predicted support for more spending from 40% to 60% (p.83-89), with no partisan/motivated-reasoning difference -- same corrective-numbers mechanism as the Funding intervention.

goldwert_2025_action_literacy.pdf.notes: Tests information about effective personal climate actions and finds improved commitments but reduced collective-action intentions.

goldwert_2026_advocacy_megastudy.pdf.notes: Tests 17 expert-crowdsourced interventions (n=31,324) for public/political/financial climate advocacy; collective-efficacy+emotional framing and binding moral-foundations framing were most effective -- multi-intervention tournament like vlasceanu_2024/voelkel_2026, not yet matched to a single named stimulus.

goldwert_2026_information_source.pdf.notes: Compares twelve information sources and finds large credibility differences but limited differences in message incorporation.

hausfather_2020_climate_model_projection.notes: Evaluates historical climate-model projections and finds that most projected subsequent warming accurately.

hautea_2024_scientist_biographies.pdf.notes: Shows that benevolence information in scientist biographies can increase perceived integrity, benevolence, and willingness to trust.

herberz_2023_partisan_framing.pdf.notes: Examines how implicit and explicit partisan cues in climate messages shape policy support.

howe_2019_uncertainty.pdf.notes: Finds that bounded uncertainty can increase trust, while acknowledging irreducible uncertainty can remove that benefit.

hoyle_2025_netzero_fairness.pdf.notes: Finds fairness perceptions strongly predict net-zero policy support and competing counterframes can neutralize pro-policy frames.

hulkkonen_2024_tailored_info.pdf.notes: Tests personalized local-impact information and finds increased knowledge with demographic-dependent policy effects.

joon_2026_climate_justice_policy.pdf.notes: Links climate-justice orientations to preferences for policy stringency, redistribution, and policy instruments.

joslyn_2016_uncertainty_communication.pd.notes: Finds that including quantified uncertainty with climate projections can increase trust in the information.

koetke_2025_intellectual_humility.pdf.notes: Finds that portraying scientists as intellectually humble increases trust, research belief, and recommendation-following intentions.

kotcher_2023_opponents_climate_action.pd.notes: Finds that identifying fossil-fuel executives or politicians as opponents can increase policy support and advocacy intentions.

macinnes_2026_trust_climate_why.pdf.notes: Shows that clarity, shared values, sincerity, and respect shape trust differently for climate believers and skeptics.

offerwestort_2026_frame_fits.pdf.notes: Compares scientific, religious, moral, efficiency, and equity frames and finds the efficiency frame performs best.

orchinik_2024_learning_scientists.pdf.notes: Tests varying consensus levels and shows that consensus information changes both climate beliefs and perceptions of scientist skill.

rabinovich_2012_communicator_motives.pdf.notes: Shows that perceived intent to inform rather than persuade can increase trust when message style matches expectations.

rinscheid_2021_social_norms_elite_cues.p.notes: Tests descriptive norms and political endorsements, finding limited norm effects and trust-dependent elite-cue effects.

rode_2026_consensus_field.pdf.notes: Field experiment finds consensus messages increase consensus estimates and climate belief but not downstream behavior.

sanz-menendez_2019_credibility_sources.p.notes: Shows that identical climate information receives different credibility depending on its institutional source.

sinclair_2025_behavioral_interventions_t.notes: Intervention tournament (n=7,624) testing 17 psychological strategies to motivate climate information-sharing and action -- multi-intervention tournament like vlasceanu_2024/voelkel_2026, not yet matched to a single named stimulus.

tiede_2026_public_engagement_norms.pdf.notes: Finds people underestimate broad support but overestimate rare behaviors, and corrections have limited behavioral effects.

vanderlinden_2015_gateway_belief.pdf.notes: Provides experimental evidence that perceived scientific consensus influences climate beliefs, worry, and support for public action.

veckalov_2024_consensus_27country.pdf.notes: Across 27 countries, consensus messages reduce misperceptions and slightly increase beliefs and worry without direct policy effects.

vlasceanu_2024_global_tournament.pdf.notes: Compares eleven interventions in 63 countries and finds small, outcome-specific effects and no increase in effortful behavior.

voelkel_2026_megastudy.pdf.notes: Large registered-report comparison finds generally small and similar persuasive effects, with no increase in donations.

wu_2025_copartisan_officials.pdf.notes: Finds co-partisan elected-official messages increase mitigation intentions without changing underlying climate beliefs.

yale_gmu_2025_politics_policy_spring.pdf.journal: Yale Program on Climate Change Communication / George Mason University CCCC
yale_gmu_2025_politics_policy_spring.pdf.notes: Climate Change in the American Mind: Politics & Policy, Spring 2025 (fielded May 2025). 79% of registered voters oppose ordering federal agencies to stop climate research (p.16-17,46); 80% support funding more renewable-energy research (p.9,40); both hold across party lines -- climate-specific baseline for funding_perceptions.
